hypotheses.reasoning: Trigger: session-cache restarted at 21:42:34 after node replacement with no RDB snapshot, so it came up with 0 keys (#224). Survivable alone, but account-svc then saw session-cache miss ratio jump to 98% vs a 4% baseline and began loading every session from accounts-db (#231, #235). That miss storm drove accounts-db connections to 488-496/500 with CPU at 94-97% (#232, #240), and queries on accounts slowed to 3-8.7s (#243). account-svc queries then hit the 5000ms timeout (#254), and edge-proxy returned 504s after 6-29s. The 504s are downstream symptoms and are not cited as origin evidence. Alternative: dependency_timeout on accounts-db, since the DB is the hung dependency; but its load is caused by cache-miss amplification, so cascading_failure fits better. The audit_log seq scan (#201), the audit-consumer GC pause (#205), and the IdP reset (#52) are not causal here.

accounts-db saturation (connections near max, CPU high, slow point lookups) causes account-svc query timeouts. This is the proximate failure mode, but it is driven by the upstream cache miss storm rather than an independent hang.

verdict.recommendedAction: Restore or warm session-cache (reload from snapshot or pre-populate keys) and enable persistence (RDB/AOF) so node replacements do not start empty. Add request coalescing or a rate limit on session-cache-miss loads to accounts-db, and temporarily shed load on account-svc to relieve accounts-db connection and CPU pressure. Then verify the miss ratio returns to baseline (~4%) and the 504 rate drops.
